bullets.text: Coal India Oct production 67.2mt (+19.1% yoy), offtake 70.3mt (+20.6%); e-auction premium 140% vs 94% in Sep; Emkay ADD, TP Rs475 unchanged.
bullets.source: Emkay - Coal India: Production recovery gains traction amid robust offtake; ADD; Target: Rs475

detail.summary: Offtake is running well ahead of production, so mine stocks are being drawn down and a 2H production catch-up is needed. Emkay thinks mining conditions support that catch-up. The jump in e-auction premium improves 2HFY27 earnings visibility, so it keeps ADD and the Rs475 TP.

bullets.text: PhillipCapital keeps Dixon SELL, TP Rs9,082 (-17% vs Rs11,000), at 40x FY28 EPS Rs227; sees H2 smartphone volumes 26% below H1.
bullets.source: PhillipCapital - DIXON TECH (DIXON IN)- Mobile biz to keep facing headwinds (PhillipCapital India)

detail.summary: Management's FY27 guide of 33-34mn units ex-Vivo needs H2 volumes only 2-8% below H1, which PhillipCapital thinks is hard because stocking is H1-weighted. It sees camera and display margins and IT hardware allocations capped, and no material Pixel uplift.

FY27 volume est 30mn ex-Vivo plus 5mn Vivo = 35mn; H2 at 12.8mn

bullets.text: Emkay keeps Dixon BUY, TP Rs16,400 (-1.8%, 49% upside); FY27E EPS cut ~21% on no PLI, FY28E EPS raised ~7%.
bullets.source: Emkay - Dixon Technologies: Resilient volumes, rising ASPs drive growth; BUY; Target: Rs16,400

detail.summary: Q2 growth came from a ~35% yoy ASP rise as memory took a bigger share of the phone BOM, with volumes 9.5mn (-7% yoy). Emkay lifts ASPs and trims PLI, so FY27 EPS falls while FY28 rises; it argues wallet-share gains offset memory-cycle volume loss.
points: TP Rs16,400 (Dec-27 DCF) vs Rs16,700 earlier; 44x FY28E PER
Q2 EBITDAM 2.7%, 26bps below Emkay estimate

detail.summary: Q2 revenue and PAT grew sharply, but gross contribution margin fell on material pass-through and a lower-margin electronics mix, and working capital and debt rose. RAC volume recovery is pushed to H2, with PLI income still to be recognised.

bullets.text: Near-frontier AI models priced at up to a fifth of frontier pricing, but CLSA sees no full price war yet.
bullets.source: CLSA - Global Technology: LLM Diaries: Pricing the frontier

detail.summary: CLSA argues the price-war fear is overstated. Near-frontier models are the battleground, while frontier pricing holds and OpenAI's old premium has gone. Anthropic's near-frontier launches raised token consumption but slowed 3Q26 revenue momentum.
points: Near-frontier priced at up to one fifth of frontier
Price per unit of intelligence down ~99.5% in three years
90% of that fall from smarter models, 10% from price cuts
AI labs ~57% of cumulative ARR in 550+ company tracker
Anthropic near-frontier launches lifted tokens, slowed 3Q26 revenue momentum
